title: TESS outburst candidates of three ZZ Ceti stars are M-dwarf flares and an asteroid; a 600-star TESS search finds 11 outbursts in 8 white dwarfs, all at 10,700-11,800 K
abstract: Question: Which TESS brightenings of cool DA white dwarfs are real ZZ Ceti outbursts, and which come from neighbours, companions or asteroids? Method: We tested the three TESS candidate outbursters of Bognar & Sodor (2026) with Gaia DR3 neighbours, PSF fits of event difference images with injection tests, minor-planet positions computed from the TESS orbit (JPL Horizons), and flare-shape fits. We then searched 3,060 SPOC 2-min light curves (Sectors 1-107) of 600 Gaia DA-candidate white dwarfs at 9,500-13,500 K with box filters, inverted light curves as a false-alarm reference, and 7,844 injected outbursts. We vetted each event. For hours-long events we tested pulsation changes against random windows with a spectral-concentration statistic, and the statistic rejects a flare control and an asteroid control. Results: Five of the six published events are flares of co-moving M dwarfs 12 arcsec from EC 11266-2217 and G 117-B15A. The PSF fits put the light on the M dwarf (chi-square difference 26-397). The sixth event (GD 842) is the asteroid (15026) Davidscott, 16.6 arcsec away as seen from TESS; the geocentric SkyBoT check misses it. The search gave 90 events at S >= 8: 39 asteroids, 11 flares (all on stars with co-moving red companions), 22 neighbours or systematics, and 14 outburst-like events. Eleven outbursts in eight stars pass our tests. Tier A (on target, coherent pulsation change, p <= 0.005): GD 1212 (2021, 2023), BPM 30551 (2025), LAMOST J072300.20+161704.4 (2023) and HE 0532-5605 (2018, 2020, 2025; the same new 2530 microHz mode in each). Tier B: four more stars. All eight have photometric Teff of 10,740-11,730 K (chance probability 2e-4). Corrected for efficiency, outbursts above 10 % occur 0.34-0.65 times per star per year at 10,300-11,800 K, and less than 0.25-0.44 times outside this range. Limitations: photometric Teff; one analyst did the visual vetting; the search is incomplete below about 5 % amplitude; the pixel test is weak for faint stars; tier-B stars need ground confirmation. For each event: light curve in 30-min bins with 2-h smoothing (shaded: event window), and pulsation amplitude spectra before (blue) and during (orange) the event. Coherent modes become stronger or appear during the outbursts.

Event difference images of the three published TESS outburst candidates. The best-fit source (red cross) lies on the co-moving M dwarf for EC 11266-2217 and G 117-B15A, and on the TESS-centric track of the asteroid (15026) Davidscott for GD 842.

Search of 3,060 TESS 2-min light curves of 600 cool DA-candidate white dwarfs: (a) events against threshold for real and inverted light curves; (b) injection recovery against amplitude and noise; (c) efficiency-corrected rate of outbursts above 10 % per Teff bin with 95 % intervals. Ticks show the 11 detected outbursts.
